purpose: NUMERIC edge-type vocabulary for the provider selection graph. An edge between two ProviderNodes carries a numeric `code` (control logic) + a `label` (display only). Numeric codes leave gaps for new edge kinds. Combined with numeric priority/cost/reliability/latency/safety WEIGHTS on each edge, this lets a new provider be inserted BETWEEN existing ones (e.g. priority 6500 between 5000 and 7000) without renumbering or code changes. See _repos/teleon/context/architecture/numeric-preference-graph.md.
control_rule: Branch on numeric edge `code` + numeric weights, never on the edge label string or a provider display name.

codes.label: EMULATES
codes.note: node is a local contract-compatible emulator of the target

codes.label: SUPERSEDES
codes.note: node replaces an older one (e.g. v2 supersedes v1)

codes.label: SHADOW_OF
codes.note: runs in shadow alongside the target; results compared, not served

codes.label: CANARY_OF
codes.note: receives a weighted slice of traffic vs the target

codes.label: FALLBACK_AFTER_FAILURE
codes.note: selected when the higher-priority node is unavailable/unhealthy

codes.label: REQUIRES_APPROVAL
codes.note: selectable only with explicit human/owner approval

weight_scale.note: Priority/score weights use a 0-10000 scale with deliberate gaps so new providers slot BETWEEN existing ones.
